    Password Reset Setup Guide

    This guide explains how to configure Supabase for the complete password reset flow.

    Supabase Configuration

    To enable the password reset functionality, you need to configure the redirect URL in your Supabase project:

    1. Access Supabase Dashboard

    1. Go to Supabase Dashboard
    2. Select your project
    3. Navigate to Authentication → URL Configuration

    2. Configure Redirect URLs

    IMPORTANT: This is the crucial step that determines where users are redirected when they click the reset link in their email.

    In the Redirect URLs section, add the following URL:

    http://localhost:3000/reset-password

    For production, replace localhost:3000 with your actual domain:

    https://yourdomain.com/reset-password

    Note: Make sure this URL exactly matches your frontend route /reset-password. This is where users will be taken when they click the "Reset password" button in the email.

    3. Configure Site URL

    Make sure your Site URL is set to your frontend URL:

    • Development: http://localhost:3000
    • Production: https://yourdomain.com

    4. Backend Environment Variable (Optional)

    For production deployments, you can set the FRONTEND_URL environment variable in your backend to ensure the correct redirect URL is used:

    # In your .env file or environment variables
FRONTEND_URL=https://yourdomain.com

    If not set, it defaults to http://localhost:3000 for development.

    5. Email Templates (Optional)

    You can customize the password reset email template:

    1. Go to Authentication → Email Templates
    2. Select Reset Password
    3. Customize the template as needed
    4. The reset link will automatically redirect to /reset-password with the required tokens

    Important: The email template will contain a "Reset password" button/link. When users click this link, they will be redirected to the URL you configured in step 2 above (/reset-password).

    How the Flow Works

    1. User requests password reset: Clicks "Forgot password?" on login form
    2. Email sent: Supabase sends password reset email with secure link
    3. User clicks link: Redirected to /reset-password with access_token and refresh_token
    4. Password update: User enters new password, which is updated via Supabase API
    5. Success: User is redirected to login page with success message

    Visual Flow Diagram

    User clicks "Forgot password?" 
         ↓
   /forgot-password page
         ↓
   User enters email
         ↓
   Supabase sends email
         ↓
   User clicks "Reset password" in email
         ↓
   Redirected to /reset-password (with tokens)
         ↓
   User enters new password
         ↓
   Password updated successfully
         ↓
   Redirected to /login

    Key Point: The redirect from the email to /reset-password is controlled by the Redirect URLs setting in Supabase. Make sure this is configured correctly!

    Security Notes

    • The reset tokens are only valid for a limited time (configurable in Supabase)
    • Tokens are single-use and expire after password update
    • The /reset-password page validates tokens before allowing password update
    • All password updates are handled securely through Supabase's authentication system

    Testing

    To test the password reset flow:

    1. Start your frontend and backend servers
    2. Go to the login page
    3. Click "Forgot password?"
    4. Enter a valid email address
    5. Check your email for the reset link
    6. Click the link to test the password update flow

    Troubleshooting

    Common Issues

    1. "Invalid password reset link" error: Check that the redirect URL is correctly configured in Supabase
    2. User redirected to landing page instead of reset page:
    3. Verify the Redirect URL in Supabase is set to http://localhost:3000/reset-password (or your production domain)
    4. Make sure the URL exactly matches your frontend route
    5. Check that there are no typos in the redirect URL
    6. IMPORTANT: The backend now explicitly sets the redirect URL when sending the email. Check the backend logs to see what redirect URL is being used

    7. Ensure your frontend is running on the correct port (3000 by default)

    8. "otp_expired" or "access_denied" error in URL:

    9. This means the password reset link has expired (usually expires in 1 hour)
    10. The page now handles this error gracefully and shows a "Request New Password Reset" button
    11. Try requesting a new password reset immediately after the error
    12. Check if your system clock is correct (timezone issues can cause early expiration)
    13. "Password update failed" error: Ensure the tokens are valid and not expired
    14. Email not received: Check spam folder and verify email configuration in Supabase
    15. Tokens not found in URL: Check that the redirect URL includes the tokens as query parameters

    Debug Steps

    1. Check browser console: Open browser dev tools and look for console logs when the password reset page loads
    2. Check backend logs: Look for the redirect URL being used when sending the email
    3. Verify Supabase configuration: Ensure Redirect URLs match your frontend URL
    4. Test the URL directly: Try accessing http://localhost:3000/reset-password?access_token=test&refresh_token=test to see if the page loads
    5. Check environment variables: Ensure FRONTEND_URL is set correctly in your backend
